subject: Action button redraws current plot when changing input

messages.author: a08511b61d1423a7
messages.subject: Action button redraws current plot when changing input
parts:
Hi,
I have a complex shiny app which essentially takes some input, does a bit of calculation and finally draws a plot. I added an action button to reduce widget input changes and redraws.

With the button, I can change widget input and the changes are not reflected in the plot until I click the button. That is good, but the issue is that the current plot is redrawn. Every time I change a widget input, the same current plot is redrawn. Only when I click the button do the changed input values appear in the plot. So, its partially working but if the plot is redrawn every time, it doesn't help computationally.

I have tried to create a demo app about this problem but I was unable to reproduce the issue. So, I thought I could explain.

My app essentially takes some input, does a bit of calculation and finally draws a plot. The plotting is the most demanding part therefore, all changes up to plotting should go as normal and the plotting is controlled by a button.

Here is the basic structure.

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
 
  fn1 <- reactive({
    # takes input
  })
 
  fn2 <- reactive({
    #check1
    if(is.null(fn1()) return(NULL))
     
      x<- fn1()
    #does some calculations
    return(something)
  })
 
  fn3 <- reactive({
    #check2
    if(is.null(fn2()) return(NULL))
      x <- fn2()
    #some more calculations
    return(something)
  })
 
  evr <- eventReactive(input$button, {
    fn3()
    })
 
  output$plot <- renderImage({
    #check3
    if(is.null(fn3()) return(NULL))
      plotvalues <- evr()
   
    #plot stuff
     
  })
})

No inputs go directly into the renderImage() function. Therefore, all variables pass through evr(). I have tried removing #check 3 but that doesn't help.

If anyone has any ideas or solutions, please let me know.
Thanks,
Roy

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Action button redraws current plot when changing input
parts:
The "if (is.null(fn3()) return(NULL)" is causing you to take a dependency on fn3.

You could remove that line and instead, after plotvalues <- evr(), check if plotvalues is null and return if so.

Better yet, remove all the checks for NULL, instead use validate/need (or with the upcoming Shiny release, you can use the new "req()" function to accomplish the same thing more concisely). Basically the way it works is, in fn1, if you're expecting input$foo to be non-NULL and you want to say "I can't continue" if that's not the case, you can do this:

fn1 <- reactive({
  validate(need(input$foo, FALSE))
  ... more code ...
})

The rest of your code should be the same except remove all the checks for NULL for fn1(), fn2(), etc. If fn1 executes while input$foo is NULL, then it and all its callers will abort silently. When input$foo is no longer NULL then the reactives will know to try again.

I also want to note that if "#plot stuff" makes calls to inputs, reactive values, or reactive expressions, then you'll want to wrap that in isolate({ ... }) as well to ensure that the action button is the only thing that can trigger plotting (well, that and resizing the browser window).

output$plot <- renderImage({
  plotvalues <- evr()
  isolate({
    ...
  })
})

However, if "plotvalues" is the only data you need, then you don't need to bother with the isolate.
